claims.evidence: NHS blood tests page: depends on the type of test; the professional arranging the test tells you if you need to prepare. Fasting leaflet and MedlinePlus cover fasting.
NHS blood tests page: preparation depends on the type of test; the healthcare professional arranging it will say.
Fasting (water only) is supported; anticoagulants as a preparation medicine was not found. Only 'do not change medicines unless a doctor says' was found.
claims.newSentence: For some tests the preparation is a period without food or drink other than water, and the person arranging the test will say if anything else applies.

claims.evidence: MedlinePlus: eating and drinking puts sugar, fat, protein and other nutrients in the bloodstream, which can change levels of substances measured.

NHS App help: results usually available within a few days, more complex tests may take a few weeks; GP surgery receives results; hospital-requested tests are queried with the hospital. 'Same day' not found.
claims.newSentence: Results usually reach the GP or hospital team, and timing varies from a few days to a few weeks depending on the test.

claims.evidence: NHS: whether you need to prepare depends on the type of blood test. 'Many do not' not stated as such.
claims.newSentence: Whether a blood test needs preparation depends on the type of test.

claims.evidence: NHS: the healthcare professional arranging your test will tell you if you need to prepare. Checking letter/asking is an instruction, removed.
claims.newSentence: The NHS says the healthcare professional arranging the test will tell you if you need to prepare.

claims.evidence: NHS hospital leaflet: fasting means no food or drink other than water for a set time.
No retrieved source says anticoagulants are paused for blood tests; pausing medicines is also potentially unsafe to state.
NHS leaflet and MedlinePlus: fasting means no food or drink except water before the test.
MedlinePlus: nutrients absorbed into the blood can change levels of substances and affect the accuracy of results.
NHS leaflet lists different fasting lengths per test; NHS: depends on the type of test.
NHS trust leaflets give different times for different tests. 'Follow your appointment instructions' reworded to avoid instructing.
claims.newSentence: NHS hospital leaflets give different lengths for different tests, so the person arranging the test can say which applies.

claims.evidence: Practice and trust pages describe fasting as water only. 'Morning of the test' not confirmed (one source says from the night before).
claims.newSentence: Practices that publish fasting advice usually mean water only.

claims.evidence: Retrieved summary: tea, coffee (including black), fizzy and sugar-free drinks usually off limits; one trust lists vaping and nicotine patches. Which exact page carries each item not isolated.
NHS trust advice: do not change your medicines unless your doctor tells you to.
NHS trust: if you have diabetes, check with your doctor before fasting. The stated reason was not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: People with diabetes are advised to check with their doctor before fasting for a test.

claims.evidence: If unsure, contact the GP surgery or testing clinic for the fasting time.
